emma: Heads-up — during the new reranker bring-up (gpt-rank-v2 int8 PTQ) we see NDCG@10 down ~2.1 pts vs fp16 baseline on the support-search eval. MRR down ~6% on short queries. Posting quick diffs and logs.
raj: Oof. Which eval slice is showing the drop? full test set or a particular slice? :eyes:
emma: Mostly short queries (<8 tokens) and code-search style queries. Long-doc slices look fine. The drop appears after we changed query/doc joiner and pushed PTQ.
dana: Did the tokenizer change too? Even small whitespace/punctuation normalization can shift token boundaries and affect reranker scores.
emma: We rolled a tiny preproc tweak to strip trailing punctuation from queries (to normalize). Diff (very small):
```
- q = q.rstrip('.,?')
+ q = normalize_whitespace(q).strip()
```
After that the average query token length decreased from 6.3 -> 5.8.
oliver: Also check PTQ config: are we using per-channel quant or per-tensor? Per-tensor PTQ on attention kernels can change ranking margin behavior.
emma: PTQ config: `calib=1000, dtype=int8, scheme=per_tensor` — I can try per_channel.
ci-bot: CI job rerank-eval/2938 failed: ndcg_regression_check triggered (>1.5pt) — https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/2938
raj: Can you paste the eval command and one failing example (query + top candidates)?
emma: Eval command and output snippet:
```
./eval_rerank --model gpt-rank-v2-int8 --dataset support-search --slice short-queries --k 10
NDCG@10: 0.641 (fp16 baseline 0.662)
Top failure example:
Query: "install k8s on ubuntu"
Candidates (top5): [docA: 0.72, docB: 0.71, docC: 0.70, docD: 0.69, docE: 0.67]
Baseline order (fp16): docB, docA, docC
Int8 order: docA, docB, docC
```
dana: The scores are very close — this smells like tie-breaking sensitivity. If quantization compresses logits, small differences flip order. We should add a soft-tie-breaker that uses token-overlap as secondary key for eval debugging.
oliver: Agree. Also check candidate truncation: are documents being truncated differently after joiner change? Context length affects attention and kv cache behavior.
emma: Current doc truncation uses `max_doc_tokens=512` after join. The joiner change moved some whitespace trimming earlier which removed newline tokens and compressed docs. I'll run an ablation with 768 and with the old joiner.
raj: Also run eval with `--no-normalize` (raw queries) and with `--tokenized-join` so we can isolate tokenization vs quant effects.
emma: Plan:
- run per-channel PTQ
- eval with old joiner + new joiner
- eval with max_doc_tokens=512/768
- run fixed-seed inference (deterministic tie-breaker)
- add token-overlap tie-break debug logging for failing queries
I'll kick these off and post results here. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Started job rerank-ablation/2940
emma: If anyone has a good small calibration set for PTQ that mirrors short-query distribution, please ping — the current calib set is generic docs and may not reflect our short-query skew.
dana: I have a curated 2k sample of short-support queries, will DM the link. :raised_hand:
raj: Great. If ablation still shows regressions after per-channel PTQ and joiner revert, we should run a head-to-head sample-level audit (manual inspection of ~50 fails) to decide rollback vs further tuning.
emma: Thanks — I'll run the ablations and upload the sample audit when ready. Will also open a small canary in prod for the int8 model behind a traffic split if things look stable after fixes.
